messages.content: Organizer confirmed the Tuesday reception is at the High Museum campus, not the block hotel. Can we finish the Atlanta flights against the Hampton hold? I need bag-drop time before 6, no rental car, and a Thursday return after the committee breakfast/lunch.

Here’s the tight comparison:
| Itinerary | Fare | Tue buffer/transfer | Thu return | Chicago arrival | Effect on Hampton |
| United nonstop ORD-ATL/ATL-ORD | $326 | ATL 2:55; MARTA to Arts Center + walk puts you at Hampton about 4:05 | 2:35 p.m.; leave Midtown about 12:35 | ORD 3:48 | Best fit; easy bag drop before 6 |
| Delta lower fare MDW-ATL/ATL-MDW | $259 | ATL 4:20; rideshare needed, bag drop around 5:20 if traffic behaves | 4:55 p.m.; plenty of margin | MDW 6:05 | Saves $67, but Tuesday is tight and you get home later |
I’d ticket United; the fare gap is small relative to the reception risk.
Does the United return still give me time to eat something Thursday, or is that pretending?

It works if lunch is quick. Breakfast ends 11:30; grab food near Hampton or at ATL, leave the hotel 12:25-12:35, and you should reach ATL around 1:15. If the committee drifts past noon, the later Delta return has more cushion.
What does the whole plan look like against the forum block?

Held Hampton is about $395. Hampton + United is about $721; Hampton + Delta is about $654. The block hotel lodging was roughly $548, so Hampton + United is still about $153 less than block + United and is easier to defend than paying the block premium.
Then let's ticket United. Economy, carry-on only, aisle if there’s one. Keep Hampton exactly as held.

Ticketed: United nonstop ORD-ATL Tuesday, arriving about 2:55 p.m., and United nonstop ATL-ORD Thursday, departing 2:35 p.m. and arriving ORD about 3:48 p.m.; economy, carry-on only, aisle requested. Hampton stays Nov. 15-17 with breakfast included, coffee listed, mini-fridge/quiet-room notes attached. No rental car; MARTA is fine on arrival, with rideshare as the backup.

messages.content: Switching gears to St. Louis: Dec. 8-10, two of us, museum timed entry Saturday at 10:30, and dinner with my cousin in the Central West End. We’ll leave Chicago after work Friday. Can you compare downtown versus Forest Park/CWE hotels, with total price and whether Amtrak or driving makes more sense? Breakfast, in-room coffee, and a mini-fridge would be useful; one queen or king is fine.

Yes—using refundable rates for Dec. 8-10:
| Hotel | 2-night total | Train/parking | Museum access | Breakfast + room setup | Dinner/cancel |
| Hampton Inn & Suites St. Louis at Forest Park | ~$418 | Better for driving; parking currently no charge | 7-10 min drive/rideshare to Saint Louis Art Museum | Breakfast included; coffee maker + mini-fridge listed; king or 2 queens | CWE/The Hill by short ride; cancel by Dec. 6 |
| AC Hotel Central West End | ~$492 incl. est. parking | Fine with car; awkward from a late train | Close to CWE; 10-12 min to museum | Coffee + mini-fridge; one king/queen; breakfast paid | Strongest restaurant access; 48-hour cancel |
| Hampton Downtown/Gateway Arch | ~$338, or ~$398 with parking | Easiest from Amtrak; parking adds about $60 | 25-35 min to museum by MetroLink plus walk/ride | Breakfast included; coffee + mini-fridge; king or 2 queens | Some walkable downtown dining; cancel by Dec. 6 |
If you drive, Forest Park Hampton is worth the premium for Saturday. If you take Amtrak, downtown is simpler and cheaper.
Can you add travel costs? Amtrak might be calmer after work, but I don’t love arriving late and then crossing town.

For two people, Amtrak looks about $170-$220 round trip, arriving at Gateway/Union Station late Friday. Downtown then stays easy; Forest Park/CWE would add a $20-$30 rideshare at that hour. Driving is roughly 4.5-5 hours plus gas/tolls around $95-$120. Parking changes the math: about $0 at the Forest Park Hampton, about $60 downtown, and roughly $50 at the AC.
Is the Forest Park Hampton meaningfully easier for the Saturday 10:30 entry?

Yes. From there, leave around 9:50 by car or rideshare and you still have a buffer. From downtown, I’d leave around 9:15 for MetroLink plus the walk or a short ride inside the park, or 9:35 by rideshare if traffic is light.
Please verify the Forest Park Hampton room details: breakfast, coffee, fridge, and one-bed setup.

For the standard king room: breakfast is included, an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge are listed, and the rate is refundable. I’d request a quiet king away from the elevator. If the king disappears, a queen one-bed room would be the clean fallback; I would not switch to two doubles without checking.
What dinner options are nearby if we don’t want to drive again Friday night?

At the Forest Park Hampton, plan on a short rideshare rather than a walk-heavy dinner: Central West End restaurants are about 8-12 minutes, and The Hill is also close. The downtown Hampton has more walkable arrival-night options, but that area can feel quieter late.
I think the Saturday ease matters more. Let’s drive and hold Forest Park Hampton, refundable. One bed, quiet room if possible.

Held Hampton Inn & Suites St. Louis at Forest Park for Dec. 8-10: refundable standard king/one-bed room, estimated $418 with taxes. Notes: quiet room away from elevator, breakfast included, in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge listed. Working plan is to drive after work Friday, use the hotel parking, take a short drive or rideshare to the Saint Louis Art Museum Saturday morning, and meet your cousin in the CWE. Downtown Hampton stays as the backup if you switch to Amtrak.
